fields.statement: The interim model is gone: internal/api/model.go's newModel, newModelSets, newModelBase, chain and their apply rules, Ctx.readLog and workspace.readLog (replaced by a notify-only log-read hook for the tests that count reads) and the tests of that code only are deleted, and the parity test compares the projection with a fresh strict fold alone

fields.reasoning: Reads of other roots (the daemon's projects, a run worktree at a gate, the web's answer) pick their own index path inside internal/api and today fall back to an empty IndexPath and the log; a fallback in cmd/rhiza would cover only the caller's root. AGENTS.md keeps cmd/rhiza a thin frame, and change set 01M7GFTS0N rebuilds cmd/rhiza's ctx.go globals next, so the fallback stays out of its way. It refines projection-no-index-fallback, which says what happens and not where.
fields.statement: The throwaway index is made where the projection opens (internal/api's openWriteIndex, under every root's reads) when the call's index path is empty or the index there cannot be opened or created, not in cmd/rhiza/ctx.go

fields.reasoning: render must write what the log says, and the index never re-reads a path it has seen, so HoldsLog is the guard against a stale projection. That fold applies the strict engine's rules, so one set of model rules still holds; rebuilding the index there instead is index work outside this change set's intent.
fields.statement: render keeps its strict fold of the log (changeset.FoldLog then model.AsIs) when the index does not hold exactly the log's entries (an entry file edited in place); only its empty-IndexPath branch goes

fields.reasoning: Every test use of readLog only counts reads, and those counts are what prove a read stays on the projection, so dropping them would lose that check. A notify-only hook keeps the check without a second way to supply the log. The hook is per Ctx, not a global counter, since global counters bumped by parallel tests made TestDaemonIdlePollSkipsFold flaky in #603.
fields.statement: Ctx.readLog and workspace.readLog, which replace the log read, are deleted; the tests that count log reads to show a read never decodes the log (daemon_fold_test.go:154, read_test.go:492 and :564) count through a hook on Ctx that only notes each disk read of the log and cannot change what is read

fields.reasoning: The arbiter's brief for this plan says that if deleting the interim path won't by itself bring inbox and check under target, a leaf profiles and fixes each, one concern per leaf, with the measuring command in its acceptance. A profiled probe of each command on the main checkout at c84997915 shows the costs above. This change set is the milestone's last one about reads, so the targets would otherwise go unmet.
fields.statement: This change set also brings rhiza inbox under 200 ms and rhiza check under 5 s (projection-targets), with one leaf each, because profiles show neither cost is in the interim model: inbox spends about half its 0.63 s decoding all 407 run journals (45 MB) in run.Store.List, and check spends its 7.35 s mostly in model.WhatIfFrom's per-change-set seed copies (about 2 s CPU), check.badLinks (1.4 s) and the entry decode (1.4 s)

fields.reasoning: Inbox uses only each journal's ID and State() (inboxItems, questionAdvice, inboxUncoveredProposals), and journals are append-only, so size and modification time show a change, the rule run.Store's in-process journalCache already uses for the daemon. A CLI call is a new process, so only a cache on disk saves the parse. Keeping it beside the runs folder shares it between worktrees, as the journals are shared.
fields.statement: rhiza inbox reads each run's State from a cache kept beside the run journals in the git common dir's rhiza folder: one record per journal holding its size, modification time and derived run.State, written atomically (a temporary file renamed over it), so a call parses only the journals that changed since the last one; a cache that is missing, damaged or of another format version is ignored and rewritten

fields.reasoning: copyNode and copyFields are about 2 s of check's CPU, paid once for each of about 48 in-flight change sets although each touches a few nodes. Copying on first write keeps the strict engine's results unchanged (strict-engine-is-spec). TestApplyInputsAreNotShared and TestApplyAccessorCopiesAreIndependent keep guarding against a what-if writing into the shared seed.
fields.statement: check's per-change-set what-if (model.WhatIfFrom over the one as-is seed) shares the seed's nodes and fields and copies a node only when an op of that what-if changes it, instead of copying every node and field per change set; the builder profiles again after that and fixes the next largest cost (check.badLinks, the entry decode) until check is within 5 s
